text: Next evening, Nib runs for his life across Mangwon's rooftops. The thing chasing him is a cat.
Through Nib's eyes: claws and yellow eyes. In rest form, he's no quicker than any small person.
He leaps a gap between buildings. So does the cat.
Back on their own roof, Jaeha rides Link, eyes shut. Seoa knows exactly who the cat is.
Seoa charts every run, because if he insists on bleeding for this, she wants numbers.
Jaeha smiles helplessly as a second nosebleed starts.
Then Nib hits the end of the leash and is yanked off his feet. A hundred and sixty metres: Link's limit.
Seoa holds a tissue to his nose and reminds him of their deal. He pushes harder anyway.
It pays off: Link level three, and a six-hundred-metre leash. Push too hard, though, and he bleeds.
The leash stretches, and Nib races toward the river, the cat two roofs behind.
He drops into the park by the Han River.
Under a bridge, by a pier with a yellow seven and a flickering lamp: a fenced tarp enclosure, cables, a cold glow.
Through Nib's eyes: a gate glowing under the painted seven, cables snaking toward it. No tape, no cones, no warning sign.
Seoa checks the official app. On paper, there's nothing under that bridge at all.
Someone guards that nothing very carefully. Two men in black patrol the fence, wearing the same pin.
Seoa knows that logo at a glance, and so would anyone in the city.
One guard swings his torch toward Nib's hiding place.
It lands on Gomi, licking her paw on the pallets as if she owns them. She's just saved Nib's skin.
Jaeha sketches it all, and a drop of his blood lands on the page.
Night falls. Seoa asks the obvious question. Jaeha answers the way he answers anything that might kill him.
Nib staggers home, furious, and Gomi strolls up after him, tail high. Seoa and Nib disagree about why.
Nib holds the high ground on the water tank. Gomi is in love.
Bomi's name for them has made it onto the official job board.
Saturday's gate is a step up from the last two: a car park drowned in black water, with one long ramp rising out of it.
Bomi goes live. Jaeha points at Nib with a look that means the deal still stands.
Something big moves just under the surface, and a sunken car rocks.
That black water is deeper than Nib is tall, so Jaeha moves the battle somewhere else.
A drip lands, and a long jaw of crooked teeth snaps at the ripples.
Jaeha flicks a pebble out, and a wake surges toward it from across the car park.
Two tests, and he knows what it is: a hunter that can't see, and a ramp it won't like.
The plan: someone splashing at the edge, a run uphill, and a goblin waiting on the pipe.
Yerin grabs his sleeve. She knows who does the splashing. Jaeha lifts her hand away. It's always been his job.
Nib perches on the ceiling pipe like a gargoyle, one hand already resting on his knives.
And Jaeha walks down alone and slaps the water, ringing the dinner bell.
The drowned hound erupts from the water: horse-sized, weed-covered, blind white eyes, violet ash leaking from its brow.
Jaeha runs, and the hound comes faster than his notes said. The bottom of the ramp is still wet.
Its jaws clamp on his left forearm and yank him off his feet.
At the top of the ramp, Yerin lunges forward, screaming.
And it starts dragging him back down toward the water, where Nib can't follow.
The pain in Jaeha's eyes turns cold. They're right under the pipe.
Overhead, amber floods Nib's eyes. Five minutes of field form, and he needs one move.
He drops onto the hound's head and drives both knives into the crack. The jaws spring open.
The hound bucks and thrashes on the wet concrete, Nib hanging on by one knife.
Bomi defends her ratings with her eyes squeezed shut. The arrow sails far over the hound.
And hits a parked car. The alarm goes off.
The blind hound whips its head toward the noise, and its brow is wide open.
Nib drives both knives down with his whole weight, and the hound bursts into ash and water.
Ash and water rain down on the ramp. The car alarm keeps shrieking.
Yerin heals the bite. Jaeha means the compliment, and Bomi is too honest to take it.
Twelve thousand people watched live, and the chat loved the flying husk, and the car even more.
Where the hound died, a violet core floats up out of the puddle. Nib only has eyes for the core.
Then a window with a price on it, about three million won, and only one button.
Jaeha points out the missing button. Nib's answer comes quickly. Maybe too quickly.
But for once, he doesn't look sure.
The core drifts into Jaeha's bandaged hand. One more thing for the notebook.
Operator level four, and room for a second summon: Nib may not be alone for long. Route Alignment is still loading.
The exchange buys the core, and Jaeha reads his share of the money twice.
That night Seoa pays the landlady herself, with a proud bow. The landlady counts it, then remembers her other complaint.
Seoa doesn't turn round. She knows the cover story, and Nib is offended by both options.
Then pork belly on the rooftop grill with everyone, and Gomi stretched out on the water tank above them.
Nib still won't eat until someone else has tried it. Seoa takes the bite, rolling her eyes.
On Seoa's laptop, for the first time, nothing is overdue. Not even the school trip.
Later, alone at the parapet, Jaeha looks toward the bridge. The money is fixed. The question isn't.
Far away, under the bridge, a faint cold glow.
Then the system finishes thinking: a new kind of boss, at Operator level four, is worth forty percent.
The meter brims, and Jaeha stares up, lips parted. His voice can reach Nib's world now, and a second slot is waiting.
His pencil falls from behind his ear.
Then one huge window, one button: a call, like the one that brought Nib. This time, Jaeha has to speak first.
The button glows in both his eyes. The Far Side is listening.
